nodes.label: bundles.py - one interface over five bundles
nodes.rationale: The whole reason Phase 3 does not drown in special cases. It absorbs three measured divergences in one place so no model, metric or experiment file ever branches on disease: influenza ships split integers and no mask arrays while dengue and Ebola ship masks; Ebola has five channels where the others have four; and meta['node_country'] is absent for influenza, so a synthesised group map keeps score.py's country-macro degenerating to the node mean rather than raising KeyError. Do not patch the .npz.

nodes.label: The windowing contract (w=20, h in {3,5,10,15}, direct multi-horizon)
nodes.rationale: An example is an origin t, not a node - the graph is consumed whole. An example's phase is decided by where its target lands, never by its input window. State this in the methods, because when scoring a test-phase target the input window legitimately contains test-period observations: that is what forecasting from a live surveillance stream means, and leakage-safety comes from elsewhere - the scaler saw only training cells and no input at or beyond t+h is ever read.

nodes.label: Refitting the scaler means rebuilding the input channel, not just the target
nodes.rationale: The sharpest trap in the phase and stated nowhere in the Phase-2 documents, because it only arises once you train. y == X[:,:,0] exactly in every bundle - both are inc_norm, written twice by _finalise. Refitting for y and leaving X[:,:,0] on the headline scaler leaks the test distribution into the model's inputs while every gate stays green, because the leakage suite runs at build time on the released bundles and cannot see what the trainer does at origin k. Write one function returning (X, y, scaler) and never touch the two separately.

nodes.label: Dengue is 98 per cent of the development corpus
nodes.rationale: A new finding for Phase 3 and distinct from the Brazilian dominance already settled - that one is within dengue, this one is across diseases: 98.5 per cent of nodes and 98.1 per cent of observed cells. Sample uniformly from the pooled corpus and the shared encoder sees influenza in roughly one update in fifty; it will not be a disease-agnostic encoder but a dengue encoder that has glanced at influenza, and the transfer claim is then unsupported by the training procedure that produced it.

nodes.label: Disease-balanced sampling [CONFIRM-P2]
nodes.rationale: Default: sample the dataset uniformly per batch, then origins within it, with square-root weighting recorded as a Week-6 ablation. The encoder must be equally at home on a 10-node US-regions graph and a 7,165-node dengue graph, because Ebola's 61 nodes resemble neither in scale - a dengue-dominated encoder has no reason to have learned anything that transfers to a small graph. Since an example is a whole-graph origin and the datasets differ in N and T, batches contain one dataset at a time; gradient accumulation over a round-robin is the simple correct implementation.

nodes.label: Ebola's query set is scored exactly once, and process is the only protection
nodes.rationale: Every hyperparameter is selected on the development diseases and then frozen. There is no technical control preventing a peek - 1,272 query cells sit in a file you can load at any moment - so until the receipt exists the rule is behavioural: ebola.npz's query mask does not enter any loop that chooses anything, not for a sanity check, not for a shape assertion, not 'just to see'.

nodes.label: run_ebola_once.py and the query receipt
nodes.rationale: Writes results/ebola_query_receipt.json with the frozen-config hash, the code hash, a timestamp and the scores, and refuses to run if that file exists; re-running requires an explicit flag and appends a new receipt rather than overwriting. The receipt is the audit trail that the query set was scored once, and it is what you show a reviewer who asks.

nodes.label: Rehearse the Ebola path without scoring it (Day 20)
nodes.rationale: Find every bug in the Ebola path while the query set is still sealed: run adaptation on the support cells, produce query-shaped predictions, assert shapes, absence of NaN and the pooled-support scaler, and compute no metric. Verify that the 52 districts with no support cell - the paper's central regime - all receive predictions, because a bug there surfacing on Day 21 costs the single evaluation.

nodes.label: The head-to-head must compare like with like, and Ebola has no fair comparator
nodes.rationale: Every baseline is single-disease by construction, so the G6 comparison is our encoder trained single-disease against baselines trained single-disease; the transfer-trained variant is a separate, additional row, because reporting it as the head-to-head would compare a model that saw four datasets against models that saw one. On Ebola no baseline can do few-shot adaptation at all, so a large margin over a comparator that cannot in principle do the task is evidence that the regime is hard, not that the model is good - the honest claim is that the framework produces usable forecasts where incumbents produce none.

nodes.label: Three environments, and the ebola-train split
nodes.rationale: The training code reads .npz and needs numpy + torch only - it never touches geometry - so forcing torch and the GEOS/GDAL/PROJ stack to co-resolve in one conda environment is a solved problem turned into an afternoon. scipy earns its place for the significance battery and nothing else; do not add a statistics framework for two tests. Hardware is an RTX 3060 with 12 GB, not the 8 GB the Phase-2 guide stated.

nodes.label: score.py extended to the full metric protocol
nodes.rationale: Extend the METRICS dict; do not rewrite the aggregation, which is the verified part. Adds sMAPE, peak intensity error and peak timing error, with CRPS/PICP/width following once intervals exist. Two existing rules the new metrics must not break: metrics are computed in count space against the bundle's raw, and genuinely constant nodes are excluded - peak timing on a constant node is undefined, so that exclusion is exactly right. The only data-layer exception to the Phase-3 code freeze, because it is a metrics module.

nodes.label: The naive sanity floors (persistence, seasonal naive, per-node train mean)
nodes.rationale: If the encoder does not beat all three on every dataset and horizon, the problem is in the harness, not the architecture. Costs an hour and has caught this class of bug in every project that has bothered.

nodes.label: Phase-3 data-code freeze and the escalation rule
nodes.rationale: to_schema.py, build_datasets.py and the leakage suite are frozen. Every number in data_audit.md is computed from these files and the manuscript quotes them, so if a bundle looks wrong that is an escalation, not a patch. The processed .npz files are read-only inputs: row i is meta['node_ids'][i] and column t is meta['dates'][t], and nothing downstream re-derives that correspondence.

nodes.label: export_baseline.py - export, do not port
nodes.rationale: EpiGNN/src, colagnn/src and HeatGNN-14DB/src each contain the same {data, layers, models, train, utils}.py structure - one code lineage consuming a [T,N] matrix plus an [N,N] adjacency, which is our bundles transposed. One ~40-line exporter covers three comparators; porting our loader into each repository would mean maintaining three forks of code we do not own. Two things must cross or the comparison is invalid: our split (the baselines' internal 50/20/30 coincides with ours on influenza but not on per-country dengue) and our mask (dengue is 21.75 per cent observed, and scoring baselines on 78 per cent fabricated zeros rigs the comparison in our favour, which is worse than losing).

nodes.label: Standardise horizons and metric definitions before any table is drawn
nodes.rationale: The reproduction record shows why this is the top threat to a SOTA claim: one model ran at h=1 against a paper reporting {2,3,5,10,15}, another reports RMSE in thousands, a third logs MAPE as a fraction where its paper prints percentage points. Fix the grid at {3,5,10,15}, save every baseline's raw predictions, recompute every metric through our score.py, and never copy a number out of a baseline's own log.

nodes.label: EpiGNN (core comparator)
nodes.rationale: Reproduced within ~1 per cent; re-run at h in {3,5,10,15} with 5 seeds.

nodes.label: Cola-GNN (core comparator)
nodes.rationale: Ran at h=1 while its paper reports {2,3,5,10,15}; must be re-run at our horizons.

nodes.label: MTGNN (non-epidemic control row)
nodes.rationale: Kept as the control row because it establishes what a general ST-GNN achieves without epidemic structure.

nodes.label: HeatGNN (units in x10^3)
nodes.rationale: Ran at h=1 and its paper reports Japan RMSE in thousands, so the units must be watched when re-running at our horizons.

nodes.label: MepoGNN - mobility-driven variant out of scope
nodes.rationale: All three of its source files reference commuting/OD data and A_mob is None for every disease, so the Dynamic variant cannot run on our data. Run the adaptive/learned-graph variant if the repo exposes one and disclose that the mobility-driven variant is out of scope for want of an OD matrix - a property of our data, not a failure of the model, and it must be stated that way.

nodes.label: STOEP - excluded pending provenance
nodes.rationale: Its paper table does not match the shipped dataset or metric. Timebox one day; if unresolved, exclude and document why - a comparator whose published numbers you cannot reproduce is not a comparator, and reporting it anyway invites the reviewer to ask which number is wrong.

nodes.label: MSGNN - not reproducible in our environment
nodes.rationale: Blocked on CUDA 10.1 / Linux. Timebox WSL2; if it does not run, report the specific blocker - a legitimate and useful finding, since the reproducibility appendix is a contribution in its own right.

nodes.label: Leave-one-disease-out zero-shot transfer
nodes.rationale: Train the shared encoder on three development datasets and evaluate on the fourth with no adaptation - the first direct evidence for G2. Report against two references: the single-disease model on the held-out dataset (the ceiling) and the naive floors, since the interesting quantity is where zero-shot sits between them. Watch for the tell: if zero-shot dengue->influenza is surprisingly strong, check that no geographic or scale information is leaking, because northern/southern-hemisphere phase is legitimate shared signal but anything beyond it deserves a second look.

nodes.label: First-order MAML (Reptile-style) over diseases as tasks
nodes.rationale: Full second-order MAML roughly triples memory for a benefit usually small at this scale, and first-order variants keep the 7,165-node dengue graph inside 12 GB. The inner loop adapts only the per-disease adapter, matching exactly what will be adapted on Ebola, with plain multi-task joint training as the meta-learning-free control. Adversarial disease-discrimination was rejected because the discriminator can trivially separate diseases by graph size, so it would learn to erase useful signal.

nodes.label: The k-shot sweep on calendar-prefix surrogates
nodes.rationale: Treat each held-out development disease as a surrogate emerging pathogen under the same calendar-prefix support construction, sweeping k, inner steps and inner LR; the curve is the headline figure for G3 - the quantitative statement of how little data the framework needs. The surrogate must be built the way Ebola's was, as a calendar prefix rather than the first k observed weeks per node, because selecting adaptation settings on an acausally-built surrogate would tune for a regime Ebola does not present.

nodes.label: configs/frozen_ebola_protocol.json (the Day-19 freeze)
nodes.rationale: Read-only after writing: encoder hyperparameters, adapter definition, inner steps, inner LR, support scheme, seeds and a hash of the code that produced them. Everything after this point reads the file and nothing writes it. Record why each value was chosen and which development fold chose it, because that paragraph is a manuscript section and is much harder to reconstruct in Week 6 than to write on the day.

nodes.label: Adaptive conformal inference (ACI) for calibrated intervals
nodes.rationale: Maintain alpha_t online along the calendar with alpha_{t+1} = alpha_t + gamma(alpha - err_t) and emit the alpha_t-level interval from the quantile head. Chosen precisely because it needs no held-out calibration set, which Ebola does not have. Cross-check against split conformal on the development diseases, which do have a validation fold: agreement there is the evidence the implementation is correct before it is trusted where no cross-check exists. Calibration must be reported per horizon, since coverage that holds at h=3 and collapses at h=15 is the normal failure mode and is a finding, not something to average away.

nodes.label: Gibbs & Candes 2021, adaptive conformal inference
nodes.author: Gibbs, Candes

nodes.label: Uncertainty under distribution shift and the zero-shot districts
nodes.rationale: The interesting calibration question is not whether PICP is 90 per cent on dengue's test fold but whether coverage survives on a held-out disease and, within it, on the 52 zero-shot districts. Widening intervals there is the correct behaviour and should be shown, not apologised for - a model that knows it is uncertain where it has no data is the calibration claim.

nodes.label: GradientSHAP explainability, scoped tightly
nodes.rationale: KernelSHAP is prohibitively expensive on a 7,165-node graph and attention weights are neither SHAP nor faithful. Global attributions per channel and per lag have a checkable expected ordering - recent lags and incidence dominate, with the seasonality channels weighing more on influenza than on Ebola, since a 52-week outbreak has no seasonal cycle to learn - and if that ordering does not appear, distrust the attribution before distrusting the epidemiology. Spatial neighbour attribution by edge ablation answers the question the paper poses: where does a forecast for a district we have never observed actually come from?

nodes.label: Significance battery (Diebold-Mariano, Friedman, Nemenyi)
nodes.rationale: DM per model pair per dataset per horizon with the Harvey-Leybourne-Newbold small-sample correction. DM operates on a series of loss differentials, so the node panel must be reduced to one value per time step before testing and that reduction stated. Then Friedman across (dataset x horizon) blocks with models as treatments, and Nemenyi post-hoc for the critical-difference diagram, on seed-averaged predictions.

nodes.label: The eight ablations, each isolating one claim
nodes.rationale: Transfer vs single-disease, meta-learning vs joint training, uniform vs country-balanced sampling, disease-uniform vs proportional, the epi-informed penalty, constant nodes in vs out, core-4 vs extended channels, and the Ebola support window. Only the support-window ablation touches Ebola, and it is a parameter variation declared in advance rather than a second bite at the query set. The core-4 ablation quantifies the price of the framework's central constraint: if withholding deaths_norm and C costs little the disease-agnosticism argument gets much stronger, and if it costs a lot that is an honest limitation a reviewer will respect being measured.

nodes.label: results/*.json - every table and figure generated, not typed
nodes.rationale: One record per model x dataset x horizon x seed x metric. Every table and figure is generated from this file by a script and no number is ever typed into the manuscript by hand, which is what makes the final consistency check mechanical rather than an act of faith.

nodes.label: manuscript_reconciliation.md - eight edits, item 1 first
nodes.rationale: Equation (4) still prints the retracted clip formula that fabricated 35.8 per cent of the Ebola target. It is a correctness defect sitting in a methods description, so it must not survive into a submitted draft - and no results table quotes it, which is the only reason it is still merely a defect and not a retraction. Apply it early so it cannot be quoted anywhere.

nodes.label: Baseline block dominates the compute budget
nodes.rationale: 4-5 models x 4 datasets x 4 horizons x 5 seeds is 320-400 runs, because unlike our direct multi-horizon encoder the baselines train one model per horizon. It is compute-bound, not developer-bound, so it launches on Day 15 and grinds through Week 4 with a Day-20 checkpoint. If the schedule slips, cut baseline seeds before baseline models - a three-seed comparison across five comparators is more defensible than a five-seed comparison against two - and log whatever is cut, because a silently truncated comparison reads as a complete one.
